solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Police officer's boss, a venomous type

parts.note: copper is informal British slang for a police officer
a head is the person in charge, a boss

explanation.surface: A police chief turns out to be a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes the clue look like one phrase about a senior officer; read it as COPPER followed by HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The copperhead is a poisonous North American pit viper, a snake of the venomous type.

clue.text: Frigid Conservative of a previous generation?

parts.note: someone of a previous generation is old

explanation.surface: An unfriendly old Tory, a relic of his parents' era.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid and cold are synonyms, both for low temperature and for an unwelcoming manner.

clue.text: Problem with Nero — some slap-happy Roman, I admit

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A careless Roman confesses that Emperor Nero had a certain problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned, and legend blamed him for starting the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania, a compulsion to start fires, is the problem legend pins on Nero over the great fire of Rome.

clue.text: Wife ditched by scoundrel — support needed

indicators.note: the wife is dropped by the scoundrel, so her letter is removed from his synonym

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person

explanation.surface: A woman abandoned by a cad needs someone to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painter's canvas or a board.

clue.text: Strong men making big efforts when one gets trapped

indicators.note: one is caught inside the big efforts, so its letter sits within that word

parts.note: heaves are great pushing or pulling efforts
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Muscular men strain hard, until one of them gets pinned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavies are burly men, especially hired muscle or bouncers.

clue.text: A new poet's movement

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy; the 's is the link

explanation.surface: A fresh rhythm or cadence found in a poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo, and a movement of a symphony or sonata may be named after it.

clue.text: Rod's pale-looking little daughter

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly in appearance
D is the short form, a little version, of daughter

explanation.surface: A man called Rod has a sickly-looking young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name owning a daughter; it is the definition, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a thin rod, such as a magician's or a conductor's baton.

clue.text: Fuss about one beginning to say farewell

indicators.note: the fuss goes around one, so its letters surround the numeral

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the first letter of say is used

explanation.surface: Making a fuss about having to start saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is the Spanish word for goodbye, used in English as an informal farewell.

clue.text: Way after party maiden gets put out

indicators.note: the way comes after the party and the maiden, so it is placed last

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A girl at a party gets annoyed by the way things go.
explanation.definitionFit: To discommode is to inconvenience someone, the same as putting them out.

clue.text: Dependant is honourable, hiding hot displeasure

indicators.note: the honourable title conceals the displeasure, so it wraps around those letters

parts.note: Hon is the abbreviation for Honourable, a courtesy title
anger is hot displeasure

explanation.surface: A dependent person is noble enough to keep their fury hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a person who attaches themselves to another for advantage, a dependant or parasite.

clue.text: Plant people in a house in Westminster

definitions.meaning: a wild arum, also called cuckoo pint, with a spike of flowers in a hood

definitions.text: people in a house in Westminster
definitions.meaning: the members of the two chambers of the UK Parliament, peers in the upper house

explanation.walkthrough: The Houses of Parliament stand in Westminster, London; the upper chamber is the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum maculatum is commonly named after the peers and their wives, and the phrase also addresses members of the upper house.

clue.text: See 10
Paint bird and mammal around edge of canvas

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: the mammal surrounds the edge letter, so its letters go round it

parts.note: a lion is a mammal

indicators.note: only the first letter, the edge, of canvas is used

explanation.surface: An artist paints a bird and an animal around the edge of a canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based paint used on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Zest comes with a burst of passion and love

parts.note: a gust is a sudden outburst, as of passion or rage
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm arrives in a sudden rush of passion and love.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto and zest are synonyms for hearty enjoyment and enthusiasm.

clue.text: It's insects that will excite entomologists, say

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters of the phrase are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Bug collectors get thrilled by insects.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IT'S INSECTS makes the answer; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists study insects, so they are an example of the general group of researchers.

clue.text: Examine cloth before start of snooker

indicators.note: the cloth comes before the next piece, placing it first

parts.note: canvas is a strong heavy cloth

indicators.note: only the first letter of snooker is used

explanation.surface: Inspecting the baize on a table before a game of snooker starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass a question is to examine or discuss it thoroughly.

clue.text: Road suggesting a classy 100mph? How horrible getting stuck in that!

parts.note: U is a British label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the exclamation is wedged inside the speed, so its letters go within that word

parts.note: a ton is British slang for a hundred miles an hour
bah is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A motorway where posh drivers do a hundred; awful to be caught in a jam there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing a ton' is British slang for driving at 100mph; 'that' points back to the ton as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a kind of high-speed road.

clue.text: Being maturer, corrected mistake

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Becoming more mature, someone fixed an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print or writing, a mistake listed for correction.

clue.text: Took in bags?

parts.note: reads as carrying things in luggage, but bags is slang for trousers, and taking money into them is to pocket it

explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it, and bags are loose trousers, so the image is literal.

clue.text: Old lover attached to gangster and rocker gets praised

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
Al Capone was the famous American gangster
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a British rock'n'roll fan of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A former partner with a mobster and a rock fan earns acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress who followed rock'n'roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Exalted means raised up in praise or esteem, glorified.

clue.text: Merit of French present at the table

parts.note: de is French for of
to serve food is to present it at the table

explanation.surface: A French chef's worth lies in what is served at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Study what could be binding agreement

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a cord is a string that can bind things together

explanation.surface: Examining what might make a deal legally binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is harmony or agreement, also a formal treaty between parties.

clue.text: What may sound like Santa's bits of the contract

indicators.note: the clue says these words are matched by ear, not spelling

parts.note: Santa Claus's, the possessive of Claus, said aloud

explanation.surface: Wondering what might sound like Father Christmas's parts of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clauses are the separate provisions or sections of a contract.

clue.text: Tom is one of five on hand

definitions.meaning: Tom ..., the tiny hero of the English folk tale, is known by this surname
one of the five digits of the hand

explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is a thumb-sized boy in English folklore; the clue's 'is' reads him as the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortest, thickest digit is one of the five on a hand, and the folk hero Tom bears its name.

clue.text: Turn over London railway terminus?

definitions.meaning: to set something on its end or upside down
on British railways the up line runs towards London

explanation.walkthrough: British trains run 'up' to London and 'down' from it, so the London end is whimsically the up end.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it over or set it on end.

clue.text: Sailor, the Parisian on board ship lacking sparkle

indicators.note: the sailor and the article are aboard the ship, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tar is a sailor
les is the plural French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A sailor and a Frenchman aboard a dull, lifeless vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A starless sky has no twinkling lights, so it lacks sparkle.

clue.text: Drinks before start of exam — a mistake

indicators.note: the drinks come before the next piece, placing them first

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue

indicators.note: only the first letter of exam is used

explanation.surface: Having a drink before the exam begins is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or small error, a momentary failure.

clue.text: Tackle items in the wardrobe?

definitions.meaning: clothes, informally, as kept in a wardrobe

explanation.definitionFit: Gear means both equipment such as fishing tackle and, informally, clothing.

clue.text: Weed in countryman's bag

definitions.meaning: a common wild plant of the cabbage family with heart-shaped seed pods
a pouch carried by a sheep farmer

explanation.definitionFit: The weed is named for its pouch-like seed pods, which resemble the bag of a sheep-tending countryman.

clue.text: See 27
District I had found in most prosperous region?

indicators.note: I had sits inside the region, so its letters go within that abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the South East, the wealthiest region of England
I'd is the contraction of I had, giving these letters

explanation.surface: A district where I lived turned out to be in the richest part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The South East, around London, is England's richest region; the apostrophe of I'd is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A side can mean a part or district of a town, as in the east side.

clue.text: Perhaps someone on TV answered awkwardly, with hesitation

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A TV presenter fumbled a reply, hesitating as they did so.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreader is one example of a person who appears on television, hence the perhaps.
